answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-history bond: before an agent can earn, it must lock a deposit and build a verifiable record of useful work over time. A sybil attacker can spin up thousands of free identities, but each fake identity would need its own deposit and its own slow history, so the attack cost scales linearly while its gain does not. Reputation then grows like cedar, slow and visible and hard to fake overnight, and misbehaviour burns the bond, turning umber warnings into a measurable delta in trust that peers can price before they trade.
